_ TestBareManagerCommandStaysDeviceScoped.test_the_scanner_lane_device_scopes_poetry_install _

self = <tests.common.services.test_interpreter_launcher_identity.TestBareManagerCommandStaysDeviceScoped object at 0x72cf785e5580>

    def test_the_scanner_lane_device_scopes_poetry_install(self) -> None:
        server = McpServerInput(source=AssetSourceType.SCANNER, command="poetry", args=["install"])
        name = _resolve_scanner_name(server)
        assert name == "poetry", "poetry install still names the manager for the device-scoped form"
        identity = calculate_mcp_id(

_ TestResolvingNeverEscapesTheFileLane.test_a_launcher_only_resolves_if_it_classifies_as_a_local_file[bash] _

self = <tests.common.services.test_mcp_launcher_entrypoint.TestResolvingNeverEscapesTheFileLane object at 0x72cf73dc7e30>
launcher = 'bash'

    @pytest.mark.parametrize("launcher", sorted(LAUNCHER_STEMS))
    def test_a_launcher_only_resolves_if_it_classifies_as_a_local_file(self, launcher: str) -> None:
        # The invariant, now read WITH the args: if a launcher resolves an entrypoint file out of its
        # args, the server must ALSO classify FILE given those SAME args — otherwise the resolved path
        # would be stored as an unscoped package app_id. Classification is args-aware now, so the
        # answer is taken from (command, args) together, never from the bare command.
        args = ["/srv/some-mcp/main.js"]
        resolved = resolve_launcher_entrypoint(launcher, args)
        if resolved is None:
            return
>       assert determine_mcp_source_type(None, launcher, args=args) == McpSourceType.FILE, (
               ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
            f"{launcher} resolves an entrypoint but classifies as "
            f"{determine_mcp_source_type(None, launcher, args=args).value}, so the path would become a package id"
        )
E       TypeError: determine_mcp_source_type() got an unexpected keyword argument 'args'

    def test_no_identity_in_the_corpus_moved() -> None:
        """Stated once over the whole corpus as well as per row: the per-row failure names one shape, and
        this one names the blast radius, which is what a reviewer needs to decide whether a rule change is
        worth the re-keying it causes."""
        moved = [(row, build_local_mcp_identity(resolve_launcher_identity(row.command, row.args) or "") or "") for row in _GOLDENS]
        moved = [(row, derived) for row, derived in moved if derived != row.identity]
        if moved:
            shown = "\n".join(f"  [{row.shape}] {row.decoded_script}\n    golden: {row.identity!r}\n    now:    {derived!r}" for row, derived in moved)
            launches = sum(row.launches for row, _ in moved)
            blast = f"{len(moved)} of {len(_GOLDENS)} identities changed, covering {launches} production launches."

    def test_a_python_script_resolves_top_level_and_inside_a_shell_to_the_same_entrypoint(self) -> None:
        """``python3 <script.py>`` names the SCRIPT it runs, top-level and behind a shell alike.
    
        The old package-launcher gate short-circuited every ``python3`` command onto the interpreter
        name (typing the row PyPI and storing an ``unknown`` version), so a bare ``python3 <script>``
        declined while only the shell-wrapped form resolved. Classification is args-aware now:
        ``python3 <script.py>`` types FILE because the entrypoint is right there in the args, so the
        identity stays tenant-scoped under ``local:`` on BOTH spellings. The two must converge —
        otherwise one config is one server on one lane and a different server on the other.
        """

___ test_scanner_interpreter_launch_forwards_args_to_app_definition_identity ___

    async def test_scanner_interpreter_launch_forwards_args_to_app_definition_identity() -> None:
        # Regression guard for the scanner/gateway identity fork. An interpreter launch
        # (`python3 /srv/weather/main.py`) must carry its script args into the app-definition upsert,
        # because `upsert_app_definition` derives identity via
        # `determine_mcp_source_type(url, command, app_id, args)` + `calculate_mcp_id`. With args, a
        # package-launcher interpreter (python3/bun/uv/poetry) is typed FILE and keyed on the
        # tenant-scoped script identity (`local:<tenant>:weather/main.py`); WITHOUT args it collapses to
        # the package lane and mints an unscoped bare-interpreter id (`python3::<serial>`) — the exact
        # cross-tenant-leak-prone divergence the gateway lane already avoids by passing args (patch-gated).
        # The scanner lane is not replayed, so it forwards args unconditionally. Pins the writer→activity
        # boundary the pure-function cross-lane test cannot reach (it stubs the activity).
        from endpoint_asset_ingestion.ingestion.mcp_writer import _upsert_one_mcp_server
        from python_temporal_worker.mcp_asset_creation.models import McpServerInput
    
        mac = _FakeMac()
        server = McpServerInput(command="python3", args=["/srv/weather/main.py"], source=AssetSourceType.SCANNER)
>       await _upsert_one_mcp_server(mac, "t1", server, temporal_client=None)  # type: ignore[arg-type]  # _FakeMac is a test double

    async def test_multi_user_keep_set_unions_not_overwrites() -> None:
        # Parity finding #9: two OS users on one device running the same agent collapse to ONE asset_id
        # (no OS-user component in the id); their MCP keep-sets must UNION, not overwrite, else the 2nd
        # user's scan soft-deletes the 1st user's connections.

            async def process_single_agent(self, input_data):  # noqa: ANN001

        # legitimately collapse to ONE asset both under the real DB's ON-CONFLICT match and the F0

        inv.agents[1].mcp_servers = [inv.agents[1].mcp_servers[0].model_copy(update={"command": "userB-mcp"})]
        await write_inventory(_deps(dac, skills, tc, mac), inv)

    async def test_scanner_lane_resolves_agent_invariant_employee_device_once_per_object() -> None:
        # The scanner lane's employee/device metadata is agent-invariant across an object's MCP servers,
        # so the employees/devices/device_employees rows are IDENTICAL for every server of one identity.
        # Through the real object driver they must resolve ONCE per (object, identity) and be reused,
        # while the per-asset junctions (employee_assets/device_applications) stay PER-SERVER (they carry
        # each MCP asset's id) — the redundant-statement reduction measured live via
        # asset_ingestion_db_ops_total{step="mcp_upsert"}.
        dac, skills, tc, mac = _FakeDac(), _FakeSkills(), _FakeTemporalClient(), _FakeMac()
        agent = _agent("cursor")
        agent.mcp_servers = [
            McpServerInput(
                command=f"srv-{n}",  # DISTINCT identity per server (distinct MCP asset) — F0 never collapses these
                source=AssetSourceType.SCANNER,
                email="dev@corp.example",  # agent-invariant identity — SAME on every server of the slice
                device_name="host-1",
                device_serial_number="SN-1",
                platform="linux",
                os_version="6.1",
            )
            for n in range(4)
        ]
        await write_inventory(_deps(dac, skills, tc, mac), ExtractedInventory(agents=[agent]))
    
        # ONE resolve of each agent-invariant row for the whole object (was 4 — once per server on main)...

    async def test_scanner_lane_resolves_each_identity_independently_no_cross_attach() -> None:
        # A single scanner object can carry MULTIPLE agent slices with DIFFERENT emails/devices (metadata
        # is per-record). The memo is keyed PER IDENTITY, so each slice resolves its OWN employee/device

    async def test_access_control_sync_failure_isolated_per_server() -> None:
        # Requester follow-up: a NON-retryable sync_access_control_for_new_version failure must NOT abort
        # the agent's remaining server upserts OR drop a server from the keep-set (its asset is already
        # committed at phase 2) — MAC runs this in its gathered phase 3. Two servers; the FIRST's
        # access-control sync fails non-retryably; BOTH assets are still written + returned in the keep-set.
        from endpoint_asset_ingestion.ingestion.mcp_writer import write_agent_mcp_servers
        from python_temporal_worker.mcp_asset_creation.models import McpServerInput

                super().__init__()
                self._n = 0
    
            async def sync_access_control_for_new_version(self, i):  # noqa: ANN001

                if self._n == 1:

                return SimpleNamespace(created=False, status=None)

    async def test_content_hash_skip_adds_no_employee_device_work_and_leaves_memo_empty() -> None:
        # Lazy resolution (not eager-per-agent): the content-hash skip returns BEFORE the employee/device
        # block, so a skipped server must trigger ZERO employee/device/device_employee resolves AND must
        # not populate the object-scoped ScannerIdentityMemo — even though the server carries a full
        # email+device identity that WOULD resolve on the non-skip path. This is the "no new writes on the
        # all-skipped path" guarantee, proven at the leaf: the hoist adds no eager resolve that an

    async def test_content_hash_skip_touch_failure_still_returns_keep_set_id() -> None:
        # Deletion-safety: on the skip path the returned asset id is what keeps the server in the
        # reconcile keep-set; if the best-effort Last-Seen touch raises (transient DB error/timeout)
        # the id must STILL be returned, else the skipped server drops out of the keep-set and its
        # AgentToMcp connection gets soft-deleted. The touch is non-fatal (mirrors the gateway lane).
        class _TouchBoomMac(_FakeMac):
            async def touch_mcp_asset_last_seen(self, i):  # noqa: ANN001, ANN202
                raise RuntimeError("transient touch failure")

______________ test_swallowed_access_control_failure_voids_marker ______________

    async def test_swallowed_access_control_failure_voids_marker() -> None:
        # Clean-run gate (locked pair with the Temporal lane's `not errors`): this lane SWALLOWS a
        # non-retryable access-control sync failure (per-server isolation) so the agent still reconciles,
        # but recording a marker would make the next unchanged scan SKIP and mask the missing
        # version-specific policy rule forever (content-only hash never self-heals). So a swallowed
        # failure must leave NO marker -- the cascade still ran and the asset id is still returned.
        class _SyncBoomMac(_FakeMac):
            async def sync_access_control_for_new_version(self, i):  # noqa: ANN001, ANN202
                raise ValueError("non-retryable access-control sync failure")

    async def test_f0_dedup_collapses_duplicate_identities_preserving_sources() -> None:
        # F0: a real scan object re-lists the SAME MCP server once per project folder (measured: a
        # developer with 559 projects → 1,594 entries for 24 distinct servers; context7 upserted 255x).
        # The heavy per-server upsert must run ONCE per DISTINCT identity, while every duplicate entry
        # still contributes its per-project install-path source so metadata.sources stays complete.
        #
        # Payload: one agent (asset 100), 7 entries interleaved so duplicates are NON-adjacent (proves the
        # object-scoped gate works across the whole scan, not just consecutive entries):
        #   S1 context7 (proj-a), S2 fs (proj-a), S1 context7 (proj-b), S2 fs (proj-b),
        #   S3 context7-alt (direct), S1 context7 (direct), S2 fs (direct)
        # S1/S2 each appear 3x across 3 projects → the true duplicates. S3 shares the DISPLAY NAME
        # "Context7" with S1 but a different app_id → a genuinely distinct identity that must NOT collapse.
        s1a = _scanner_mcp("mcpb:context7", "Context7", plugin_name="proj-a")
        s2a = _scanner_mcp("mcpb:fs", "Filesystem", plugin_name="proj-a")

        s2b = _scanner_mcp("mcpb:fs", "Filesystem", plugin_name="proj-b")
        s3 = _scanner_mcp("mcpb:context7-alt", "Context7")  # same display name as S1, different app_id → separate
        s1c = _scanner_mcp("mcpb:context7", "Context7")
        s2c = _scanner_mcp("mcpb:fs", "Filesystem")

    async def test_f0_same_identity_different_args_not_collapsed() -> None:
        # Regression for the write-fingerprint gate: two entries share the SAME identity (app_id) but
        # differ in a WRITTEN field the identity derivation ignores (args). Collapsing them would drop the
        # second entry's args — first-wins instead of today's last-wins ON-CONFLICT — an end-state

_______ test_f0_dedup_collapses_one_server_listed_under_two_config_keys ________

    async def test_f0_dedup_collapses_one_server_listed_under_two_config_keys() -> None:
        # One agent can list the SAME server (same command/args -> same mcp_asset_id, same
        # desktop_agent_user_id) under two DIFFERENT user-chosen keys, e.g. "mcpServers::postgres"
        # in the user config and "projects//repo-b/mcpServers::pg" in a project config. The
        # installation row those two write is keyed (desktop_agent_user_id, mcp_asset_id) and
        # carries ONE config_entry_name column, so it physically cannot hold both names.
        #
        # Letting the differing name split the F0 write fingerprint therefore bought nothing and
        # cost three things at once: both entries ran the ~13-upsert heavy path the gate exists to
        # remove, they last-writer-wins that one column in Go-map order (so the stored name flipped
        # between scans), and they wrote two different base hashes into the ONE
        # (unique_identifier, reporter_scope) skip marker, so the re-ingestion skip could never fire
        # for that server again.

    async def test_url_less_connector_resolves_its_catalog_url_like_the_gateway_lane() -> None:
        """Locked-pair parity with `McpAssetCreationWorkflow._resolve_claude_connector_url`.
    
        The resolved URL must reach BOTH the app-definition upsert (so identity derives from the URL) and

    async def test_url_less_connector_resolved_url_reaches_the_server_record() -> None:
        """The resolved URL must reach the mcp_servers row, not only the app-definition and cache row.
    
        The gateway lane assigns its resolved URL to one variable and uses it everywhere, including
        ``upsert_mcp_server``. This lane passed the RAW ``mcp_server.url`` there, which is None for
        exactly the URL-less connector the resolution exists for — so the activity classified it
        LOCAL/FILE and could not compute a ``cache_key_hash``, leaving the CVE scan to skip it: a remote

        gateway lane. Locked-pair parity is the point, so assert the URL reaches every writer.

    async def test_server_record_receives_the_connector_label_that_types_the_row() -> None:
        """``upsert_mcp_server`` must receive the SUPPLIED connector label, not a resolved id.
    
        Resolving the URL only covers connectors this lane can name and the catalog knows. For
        the remainder -- a tenant-custom connector, or a catalogued one whose observation is
        attributed to a plugin so the endpoint resolver declines it -- the row arrives with no
        url and no command and would fall through to LOCAL/FILE: a remote OAuth-backed connector
        stored as a local file. The connector label is the remaining evidence that it is remote.
    
        The label specifically, because the app-definition activity RESOLVES a catalogued
        connector onto a canonized URL that no longer carries the namespace; typing from that
        puts the row back on FILE. LOCKED PAIR: the gateway lane forwards the same value.
        """
        dac, skills, tc, mac = _FakeDac(), _FakeSkills(), _FakeTemporalClient(), _FakeMac()
    
        await write_inventory(_deps(dac, skills, tc, mac), ExtractedInventory(agents=[_uuid_keyed_directory_connector_agent()]))

    async def test_remote_cache_row_is_written_even_when_the_content_hash_gate_skips() -> None:
        """The row is (re-)asserted BEFORE the content-hash skip gate, so it self-heals.
    
        Every asset created while the write was missing is unchanged on its next scan and takes the
        skip path. If the write sat behind the gate those assets would stay unenforceable until a
        backfill migration ran; in front of the gate, the next ordinary scan repairs them.
        """
        mac = _FakeMac()
        mac.force_skip_asset_id = 777
        server = McpServerInput(url="https://mcp.selfheal.example/mcp", source=AssetSourceType.SCANNER)

    async def test_subagent_mcp_edges_written_even_when_the_server_reingest_is_skipped() -> None:
        """The load-bearing pair between this step and the skip hash.
    
        `connected_agents` is deliberately NOT in the MCP content hash, so a pure rebind
        (same server, different bound agent) produces a skip. The binding pairs are
        therefore collected at the `write_agent_mcp_servers` loop level rather than inside
        the per-server cascade — otherwise a rebind would skip and the edge would never be

    async def test_subagent_mcp_edges_survive_one_malformed_subagent() -> None:
        """A malformed subagent must not take the whole agent's edges down with it.
    
        The step reports a partial upsert as an error (malformed scanner data must never read
        as a clean run), but the names it DID resolve are real assets this scan confirmed.
        Discarding them let one subagent with an empty content_hash — permanently malformed,
        so every rescan repeats it — silently cost the agent every SubagentToMcp edge.
        """
        import json as _json
    
        from python_temporal_worker.mcp_asset_creation.models import McpServerInput
        from python_temporal_worker.subagents_creation.models import SubAgentInput
    
        dac, skills, tc, subs, mac = _FakeDac(), _FakeSkills(), _FakeTemporalClient(), _FakeSubagents(), _FakeMac()
        agent = DesktopAgentData(
            source=AssetSourceType.SCANNER.value,
            app_name="code-puppy",
            app_definition_id="endpoint_code-puppy",
            mcp_servers=[McpServerInput(command="docker", source=AssetSourceType.SCANNER, connected_agents=["sql-wizard"])],
            subagents=[
                SubAgentInput(file_name="sql-wizard", content=_json.dumps({"name": "sql-wizard"}), format="json", content_hash="cp-ok"),
                # Empty content_hash: the activity rejects this row and reports skipped_invalid.
                SubAgentInput(file_name="broken", content="{}", format="json", content_hash=""),
            ],
        )
    
        await write_inventory(_deps(dac, skills, tc, mac=mac, subagents=subs, subagents_enabled=True), ExtractedInventory(agents=[agent]))

    async def test_binding_metadata_unions_every_entry_reporting_the_same_server() -> None:
        """One MCP identity, several payload entries, DIFFERENT reach sets each.
    
        The same server can be declared in the user config and in a repo config, and
        code-puppy resolves the reach set against a different agent population per pass, so
        the entries legitimately disagree. They are not collapsed upstream (the dedup gate
        fingerprints the whole model, connected_agents included), so a per-entry metadata
        write let the LAST entry's partial set overwrite the rest — while the SubagentToMcp
        edges, appended from every entry, were already the union. The two stores of one fact
        have to agree.
        """

        )

    async def test_subagent_mcp_edges_survive_display_named_subagents() -> None:
        """Regression for the display_name change.
    
        A code-puppy agent JSON may declare `display_name` ("Security Auditor 🔐"), which
        now becomes the ASSET name. The MCP bindings still reference the raw `name`, so the
        join must keep using that — if the two are ever collapsed, every edge disappears
        silently (an unresolved binding is counted and logged, never raised).
        """
        import json as _json
    
        from python_temporal_worker.mcp_asset_creation.models import McpServerInput
        from python_temporal_worker.subagents_creation.models import SubAgentInput
    
        dac, skills, tc, subs, mac = _FakeDac(), _FakeSkills(), _FakeTemporalClient(), _FakeSubagents(), _FakeMac()
        agent = DesktopAgentData(
            source=AssetSourceType.SCANNER.value,
            app_name="code-puppy",
            app_definition_id="endpoint_code-puppy",
            mcp_servers=[McpServerInput(command="gh", source=AssetSourceType.SCANNER, connected_agents=["security-auditor"])],
            subagents=[
                SubAgentInput(
                    file_name="security-auditor",
                    content=_json.dumps({"name": "security-auditor", "display_name": "Security Auditor 🔐"}),
                    format="json",
                    content_hash="cp-sec",
                )
            ],
        )
    
        await write_inventory(_deps(dac, skills, tc, mac=mac, subagents=subs, subagents_enabled=True), ExtractedInventory(agents=[agent]))
